reader.requirement: At 1985, END PROGRAM program-name must end the program its name designates: everything after it belongs to no part of that program (its names, data and procedures are out of scope), so the next COBOL text must open a separately compiled program (IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header, required at 1985) or, for a contained program, continue the container; the witness covers the nested (Inter-Program Communication) layout, not two separately compiled Nucleus programs in one source.

edition-consulted.switches: identification-header-optional-2002: a unit after END PROGRAM opening on PROGRAM-ID without the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header is refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)
nothing: the EditionContext is only the diagnostic sink; the end-marker screen is the same at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep EndProgramHeader across src (only EndMarkerPass); grep Edition|DialectLevel in EndMarkerPass.cs (only Report's sink). The grammar's programUnit/nestedProgram pairing is edition-free.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the end itself; at 1985 the following unit must carry the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header (2002 made it optional) and END FUNCTION has no 1985 form
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c08 covers nested programs; not exercised: two separately compiled programs in one source reusing names, text after the last END PROGRAM, a header-less following unit at 85, END FUNCTION, a mismatched name

reader.notes: The grammar closes a programUnit at its endProgramHeader, so text after it is either a new unit or a syntax error, and EndMarkerPass checks the marker names the unit it closes. Behaviour conforms at --std 85. The refusals cite ISO §2023:10.7.3 at --std 85, not the 1985 rule; that is a citation-wording point on the syntax rules, not a GR1 defect.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-011/c5 (--std 85): END PROGRAM "EPA" (literal; 1985 SR1 user-defined word) refused COBOL5506; END PROGRAM epa for PROGRAM-ID EPA accepted and runs A/B (lowercase equivalent); END PROGRAM EPA without its period refused COBOL0307; a following unit opening 'ID DIVISION.' refused COBOL0001 (GR2 requires the Identification Division header); the well-formed pair runs A, B. Residual (as the reader noted): the refusals cite §2023 text at --std 85, a diagnostic-wording point, not GR1 behaviour. OK  §1985:VI.2.4.4 GR1 the text is in GR1; OK  §1985:VI.2.4.3 SR1 the text is in SR1.
